prompt: Write a PowerShell script that checks a Windows 10/11 host for common persistence mechanisms: (1) Run/RunOnce registry keys, (2) Scheduled Tasks with odd triggers, (3) Startup folder contents, (4) WMI Event Subscriptions, (5) Services with non-Microsoft signatures, (6) COM hijacking candidates in HKCU. Output a unified CSV. Add comments explaining each mechanism and what makes a finding 'suspicious'.

result.content:
```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    PersistenceMechanismAudit.ps1
.DESCRIPTION
    Audits a Windows 10/11 host for six common persistence mechanisms and
    exports findings to a unified CSV file.

    Persistence Mechanisms Covered:
      1) Run / RunOnce Registry Keys
      2) Scheduled Tasks with Suspicious Triggers
      3) Startup Folder Contents
      4) WMI Event Subscriptions (Permanent)
      5) Services with Non-Microsoft Signatures
      6) COM Hijacking Candidates in HKCU

    Each finding includes a "SuspiciousReason" column explaining WHY it
    is considered noteworthy, so the analyst can triage quickly.

.NOTES
    Run this script as Administrator for full visibility.
    Some checks (e.g., service signature validation) require the file to
    be present on disk; missing binaries are flagged separately.
#>

#Requires -RunAsAdministrator
Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CONFIGURATION
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
$OutputCsv = Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath "PersistenceAudit_$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd_HHmmss').csv"
$Results   = [System.Collections.Generic.List[PSCustomObject]]::new()

# Helper: add a row to the results list
function Add-Finding {
    param(
        [string]$Mechanism,
        [string]$RegistryPath,
        [string]$ItemName,
        [string]$ItemValue,
        [string]$TargetPath,
        [string]$SuspiciousReason,
        [string]$AdditionalInfo
    )
    $Results.Add([PSCustomObject]@{
        Timestamp        = (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')
        Hostname         = $env:COMPUTERNAME
        Mechanism        = $Mechanism
        RegistryPath     = $RegistryPath
        ItemName         = $ItemName
        ItemValue        = $ItemValue
        TargetPath       = $TargetPath
        SuspiciousReason = $SuspiciousReason
        AdditionalInfo   = $AdditionalInfo
    })
}

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1) RUN / RUNONCE REGISTRY KEYS
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
<#
  WHAT IT IS:
    The Run and RunOnce keys are the most classic Windows persistence
    mechanism.  Every time a user logs on (Run) or the next time they
    log on (RunOnce), Windows executes the commands stored in these
    registry values.

  WHAT MAKES A FINDING SUSPICIOUS:
    • The target executable lives outside standard Windows directories
      (e.g., in AppData, Temp, or a user-writable location).
    • The value points to a script (.ps1, .bat, .vbs, .js, .wsf).
    • The value contains obfuscated commands (base64, string concatenation).
    • The publisher is unknown or the binary is unsigned.
    • A RunOnce key that has NOT been cleaned up after execution (stale).
#>
Write-Host "`n[*] Checking Run / RunOnce registry keys..." -ForegroundColor Cyan

$RunKeys = @(
    @{ Hive = 'HKLM'; Path = 'SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' },
    @{ Hive = 'HKLM'; Path = 'SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce' },
    @{ Hive = 'HKCU'; Path = 'SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' },
    @{ Hive = 'HKCU'; Path = 'SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce' },
    # 64-bit views on 64-bit systems
    @{ Hive = 'HKLM'; Path = 'SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' },
    @{ Hive = 'HKLM'; Path = 'SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce' }
)

foreach ($key in $RunKeys) {
    $fullPath = "Registry::$($key.Hive):\$($key.Path)"
    try {
        $entries = Get-ItemProperty -Path $fullPath -ErrorAction Stop
        $valueNames = $entries.PSObject.Properties |
            Where-Object { $_.Name -notin @('PSPath','PSParentPath','PSChildName','PSDrive','PSProvider') }

        foreach ($prop in $valueNames) {
            $valData  = [string]$prop.Value
            $valName  = $prop.Name
            $isSuspicious = $false
            $reason      = ''

            # --- Heuristic checks ---
            # 1) Path in user-writable locations
            if ($valData -match '(?i)(?:AppData|Temp|Users\\[^/\\]+\\(?:Desktop|Downloads|Documents))') {
                $isSuspicious = $true
                $reason += "Target path in user-writable directory; "
            }
            # 2) Script file extensions
            if ($valData -match '\.(ps1|bat|cmd|vbs|js|wsf|ps2|reg|inf|scf)$') {
                $isSuspicious = $true
                $reason += "Points to a script file (.ps1/.bat/.vbs/.js/etc.); "
            }
            # 3) Obfuscation indicators
            if ($valData -match '(?i)(?:powershell.*-enc|powershell.*-e\s|base64|invoke-expression|iex\s)') {
                $isSuspicious = $true
                $reason += "Contains obfuscated PowerShell command; "
            }
            # 4) RunOnce that still exists (stale — may indicate failed cleanup)
            if ($key.Path -match 'RunOnce' -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $valData -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
                $isSuspicious = $true
                $reason += "RunOnce entry still present on disk (stale/not cleaned up); "
            }
            # 5) Non-Microsoft signed binary (best-effort)
            if ($isSuspicious -eq $false -and $valData -match '^\s*[^\s]') {
                $exePath = ($valData -split '\s+')[0].Trim('"')
                if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $exePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
                    $sig = Get-AuthenticodeSignature -FilePath $exePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
                    if ($sig.Status -ne 'Valid') {
                        $isSuspicious = $true
                        $reason += "Binary is not validly signed by Microsoft; "
                    }
                }
            }

            if ($isSuspicious) {
                Add-Finding -Mechanism 'Run/RunOnce Registry' `
                            -RegistryPath $fullPath `
                            -ItemName $valName `
                            -ItemValue $valData `
                            -TargetPath ($valData -split '\s+')[0].Trim('"') `
                            -SuspiciousReason $reason.Trim('; ') `
                            -AdditionalInfo "Run/RunOnce keys execute on user logon or once per logon respectively."
            }
        }
    }
    catch {
        Write-Verbose "Could not access $fullPath : $_"
    }
}

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 2) SCHEDULED TASKS WITH SUSPICIOUS TRIGGERS
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
<#
  WHAT IT IS:
    Windows Task Scheduler allows tasks to be triggered by many events:
    logon, boot, idle, session connect/disconnect, time-based, event
    log triggers, etc.  Malware frequently abuses Task Scheduler because
    it can run with elevated privileges and at arbitrary times.

  WHAT MAKES A FINDING SUSPICIOUS:
    • Triggers on user logon (Logon) — especially for non-Microsoft
      executables in user-writable paths.
    • Triggers on system boot (Boot) — runs with SYSTEM privileges.
    • Triggers at unusual hours (e.g., 02:00–04:00) — common for
      "living-off-the-land" attacks to avoid detection.
    • Actions that launch scripts (.ps1, .bat, .vbs, .js, .wsf).
    • Actions that launch binaries from AppData, Temp, or Public folders.
    • Tasks registered under \Microsoft\Windows but with modified
      actions (tampered system tasks).
    • Tasks with no publisher / unsigned binaries.
    • Tasks that are disabled but still have suspicious actions
      (attacker may re-enable later).
#>
Write-Host "[*] Checking Scheduled Tasks for suspicious triggers..." -ForegroundColor Cyan

try {
    $allTasks = Get-ScheduledTask -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.TaskPath -notmatch '\\Microsoft\\' -or $_.State -ne 'Disabled' }

    foreach ($task in $allTasks) {
        $taskInfo  = $task | Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        $actions   = $task.Actions
        $triggers  = $task.Triggers

        foreach ($trigger in $triggers) {
            $triggerType = $trigger.CimClass.CimClassName
            $isSuspicious = $false
            $reason      = ''

            # --- Trigger-based suspicion ---
            switch -Wildcard ($triggerType) {
                '*Logon*' {
                    $isSuspicious = $true
                    $reason += "Triggered on user logon; "
                }
                '*Boot*' {
                    $isSuspicious = $true
                    $reason += "Triggered on system boot (runs as SYSTEM); "
                }
                '*SessionStateChange*' {
                    $isSuspicious = $true
                    $reason += "Triggered on session state change (can fire on unlock/lock); "
                }
                '*TimeTrigger*' {
                    # Check for unusual hours (between 01:00 and 05:00)
                    if ($trigger.StartBoundary -match 'T(0[1-4]|05:00)') {
                        $isSuspicious = $true
                        $reason += "Time-based trigger at unusual hour ($($trigger.StartBoundary)); "
                    }
                    # Also flag if it's a one-time or daily trigger with no end date far in the future
                    if ($trigger.EndBoundary -and $trigger.EndBoundary -gt (Get-Date).AddYears(5)) {
                        $reason += "Trigger has a very far-future end date; "
                    }
                }
                '*EventTrigger*' {
                    $isSuspicious = $true
                    $reason += "Event-log-based trigger (can be used for stealthy persistence); "
                }
            }

            # --- Action-based suspicion ---
            foreach ($action in $actions) {
                $actionPath = ''
                if ($action -is [Microsoft.Management.Infrastructure.CimInstance]) {
                    $actionPath = $action.Execute
                }
                elseif ($action -is [Microsoft.Win32.ScheduledTasks.ExecAction]) {
                    $actionPath = $action.Path
                }

                if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($actionPath)) { continue }

                # Script files
                if ($actionPath -match '\.(ps1|bat|cmd|vbs|js|wsf|ps2|reg|inf)$') {
                    $isSuspicious = $true
                    $reason += "Action launches a script file; "
                }
                # User-writable paths
                if ($actionPath -match '(?i)(?:AppData|Temp|Public|ProgramData\\[^M])') {
                    $isSuspicious = $true
                    $reason += "Action target in user-writable directory; "
                }
                # Non-Microsoft signed
                if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $actionPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
                    $sig = Get-AuthenticodeSignature -FilePath $actionPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
                    if ($sig.Status -ne 'Valid') {
                        $isSuspicious = $true
                        $reason += "Action binary is not validly signed; "
                    }
                }
            }

            if ($isSuspicious) {
                Add-Finding -Mechanism 'Scheduled Task (Suspicious Trigger)' `
                            -RegistryPath "Task Scheduler\$($task.TaskPath)$($task.TaskName)" `
                            -ItemName $task.TaskName `
                            -ItemValue $triggerType `
                            -TargetPath ($actions | ForEach-Object { if ($_ -is [Microsoft.Management.Infrastructure.CimInstance]) { $_.Execute } else { $_.Path } }) -join '; ' `
                            -SuspiciousReason $reason.Trim('; ') `
                            -AdditionalInfo "Task State: $($task.State). Triggers: $($triggers.Count). Actions: $($actions.Count)."
            }
        }
    }
}
catch {
    Write-Warning "Scheduled Task enumeration failed: $_"
}

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 3) STARTUP FOLDER CONTENTS
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
<#
  WHAT IT IS:
    The Startup folders are shell folders that Windows automatically
    creates shortcuts (.lnk) or direct files in for every user and for
    all users.  Anything placed here runs when the user logs on.

  WHAT MAKES A FINDING SUSPICIOUS:
    • Shortcuts (.lnk) pointing to executables in user-writable paths.
    • Direct executable files (not shortcuts) in the startup folder.
    • Shortcuts with hidden/obfuscated target paths.
    • Files with unusual extensions (.bat, .vbs, .ps1, .js, .wsf).
    • Shortcuts whose target does not exist (broken — may have been
      planted and then the binary deleted to evade detection).
    • Shortcuts whose working directory or arguments are suspicious.
#>
Write-Host "[*] Checking Startup folder contents..." -ForegroundColor Cyan

$StartupFolders = @(
    [Environment]::GetFolderPath('CommonStartup'),   # All Users
    [Environment]::GetFolderPath('Startup')          # Current User
)

foreach ($folder in $StartupFolders) {
    if (-not (Test-Path $folder)) { continue }

    $items = Get-ChildItem -Path $folder -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    foreach ($item in $items) {
        $isSuspicious = $false
        $reason      = ''
        $targetPath  = ''

        if ($item.Extension -eq '.lnk') {
            # Resolve the shortcut target
            try {
                $shell   = New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell
                $shortcut = $shell.CreateShortcut($item.FullName)
                $targetPath = $shortcut.TargetPath

                # Broken shortcut

                    $isSuspicious = $true
                    $reason += "Shortcut target does not exist (broken/planted); "

                # Script files
                if ($targetPath -match '\.(ps1|bat|cmd|vbs|js|wsf|ps2)$') {
                    $isSuspicious = $true
                    $reason += "Shortcut targets a script file; "
                }
                # User-writable paths
                if ($targetPath -match '(?i)(?:AppData|Temp|Public)') {

1. **Run/RunOnce registry keys** - Check HKLM and HKCU for software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and RunOnce
2. **Scheduled Tasks with odd triggers** - Find scheduled tasks with triggers like logon, boot, time-based at odd hours, etc.
3. **Startup folder contents** - Check both All Users and Current User startup folders
4. **WMI Event Subscriptions** - Check for permanent WMI event consumers and bindings
5. **Services with non-Microsoft signatures** - Find services whose binary isn't signed by Microsoft
6. **COM hijacking candidates in HKCU** - Check for missing CLSID entries in HKCU that exist in HKLM (potential COM hijacking)
